chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Amr ibn Uthman from Hanan ibn Sadir from his father from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about fasting the Day of Arafah, and I said, 'May I be your ransom, they claim that it equals the fasting of a year.' He said, 'My father did not fast it.' I said, 'And why is that?' He said, 'Indeed, the Day of Arafah is a day of supplication and asking, and I fear that it will weaken me from supplication, and I dislike that I fast it, and I fear that the Day of Arafah might be the Day of Eid (Al-Adha), so it is not a day of fasting.'

key_terms.صَومُ يَومِ عَرَفَةَ: Fasting of the Day of Arafah

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Baqir not fast on the Day of Arafah?
ai.summary: This narration from al-istibsar highlights the Shia scholarly preference for prioritizing active supplication (dua) over fasting on the Day of Arafah, viewing the day as a time for petition rather than physical abstinence. Imam al-Baqir’s caution regarding potential weakness in prayer and the possibility of the day coinciding with Eid al-Adha reflects a nuanced juristic approach to maximizing spiritual benefit. This perspective underscores the Shia emphasis on the quality of worship and the specific spiritual character of the day as a time of divine acceptance.
